newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela judge postpones tanker ban for 5 years.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela judge postpones tanker ban for 5 years.

text.p: A Venezuelan judge has postponed for five years a controversial ban on single-hulled oil tankers entering the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel, according to a shipping source close to events.
The source said he obtained a copy of a letter from judge Ricardo Colmenares to the president of the state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela, Luis Giusti.

"This tribunal has reconsidered the... judiciary measure taken by this court on 3.16.97 and in this respect accorded a time period of five years from this very date for the abstention of chartering and or sale of oil and its derivatives to ships which lack double-hulls and which utilise the navegation channel of Lake Maracaibo."
The shipping source cited the letter as saying.

Judge Ricardo Colmenares banned single-hulled oil tankers from using the shipping channel effective from April 16 after the single-hulled tanker Nissos Amorgos went aground on February 28 spilling 25,000 barrels of oil.
PDVSA had asked the judge to reconsider on the basis that only about 20 percent of the world's tanker fleet has double hulls.
